title: Getting Started: Your First Five Moves in Paper Organization
summary: Start paper organization this week with five concrete moves.
body:
Don't try to do everything. Do these five, in order:

1. Gather every paper pile into one inbox
2. Sort: act / file / shred
3. Set up a simple filing system
4. Scan and back up vital documents
5. Shred the discard pile

Five moves, one week. Momentum beats perfection — the rest of this guide builds on exactly this start.

title: Common Paper Organization Mistakes and How to Avoid Them
summary: The mistakes everyone makes with paper organization — and the fixes.
body:
The classic errors:

- Filing without purging → Fix: address it in your first week, not after it costs you.
- No shredding (identity theft) → Fix: address it in your first week, not after it costs you.
- Keeping every manual (they're online) → Fix: address it in your first week, not after it costs you.
- Multiple inboxes → Fix: address it in your first week, not after it costs you.

Every mistake above is cheap to prevent and expensive to repair. Prevention is the whole game.

title: Paper Organization: Safety, Legal, and Fine Print
summary: What to watch out for with paper organization: safety, contracts, and fine print.
body:
Read before you act: Filing without purging And: No shredding (identity theft)

General rules: get agreements in writing, understand what you're signing, keep records of money in and out, and know when a professional (lawyer, accountant, vet, doctor — depending on the domain) is worth the fee. An hour of professional advice beats a month of fixing.
